title: How to check your tire pressure
metaDesc: How to check tire pressure: check cold tires once a month, use the number on the driver's door label (not the tire), add air, and do the penny test.
first: Check when the tires are cold: the car hasn't been driven for 3 hours.
Use the pressure on the label in the driver's door frame or in your owner's manual, not the number on the tire.
Check all four tires and the spare once a month.
A tire with a bulge, a cut or cords showing: don't drive on it.
dont: Don't fill to the number on the tire's sidewall. That's the most the tire can hold, not what your car needs.

steps.t: Open the driver's door and find the tire label on the door edge or frame. It lists the front and rear pressure in PSI. It's also in the owner's manual.
Unscrew the small cap on the tire's valve stem and keep it somewhere safe.
Press the tire gauge straight onto the valve stem until the hissing stops, and read the number.
Add air in short bursts at an air pump, then check again. If you add too much, press the small pin in the valve to let some out.
Screw the cap back on. Then do the other tires and the spare.
Put a penny in the tread with Lincoln's head upside down and facing you. If you can see the top of his head, the tire needs replacing.
Tire pressure drops when it gets colder outside, so check more often in winter.

call: If a tire keeps losing air, or the tire light stays on after you fill the tires, have it checked soon.
